chapters.title: I Have Loved You
chapters.html:
Malachi 1

Jacob and Esau

1The oracle. The word of the LORD to Israel through Malachi.

2"I have loved you," says the LORD. But you say, "How have You loved us?" "Was not Esau Jacob's brother?" declares the LORD. "Yet I loved Jacob,

3but Esau I hated; I have made his mountains a desolation and given his inheritance to the jackals of the wilderness."

4If Edom says, "We are shattered, but we will rebuild the ruins," this is what the LORD of hosts says: "They may build, but I will tear down. They will be called the Territory of Wickedness, the people with whom the LORD is indignant forever."

5Your own eyes will see it, and you will say, "The LORD is great beyond the territory of Israel!"

Blemished Offerings

6"A son honors his father, and a servant his master. If I am a father, where is My honor? If I am a master, where is the fear of Me?" says the LORD of hosts to you, priests, who despise My name. But you say, "How have we despised Your name?"

7"By offering defiled food on My altar." But you say, "How have we defiled You?" "By saying that the table of the LORD may be despised.

8When you offer the blind for sacrifice — 'Nothing wrong!' When you offer the lame and the sick — 'Nothing wrong!' Offer it, please, to your governor; will he be pleased with you, or show you favor?" says the LORD of hosts.

9"So now, plead with God to be gracious to us. With such offerings from your hands, will He show favor to any of you?" says the LORD of hosts.

10"Oh, that one of you would shut the doors, so that you would not light My altar for nothing! I have no pleasure in you," says the LORD of hosts, "and I will not accept an offering from your hands.

11For from the rising of the sun to its setting My name is great among the nations; in every place incense is offered to My name, and a pure offering; for My name is great among the nations," says the LORD of hosts.

12"But you profane it by saying that the table of the Lord is defiled, and its fruit, its food, may be despised.

13You say, 'What a weariness!' and you sniff at it," says the LORD of hosts. "You bring what was stolen, the lame and the sick; this is the offering you bring. Should I accept it from your hands?" says the LORD.

14"Cursed is the cheat who has a male in his flock and vows it, but sacrifices a ruined one to the Lord. For I am a great King," says the LORD of hosts, "and My name is feared among the nations."

Notes

  • v1 "The oracle… through Malachi" — massa, oracle, as in Zechariah 9:1 and 12:1. Be-yad, word for word by the hand of, is through. Mal'akhi, Malachi, means My messenger, the word the LORD uses in 3:1; the Greek has by the hand of His messenger, and adds Set it on your hearts. No father or date is given.

  • vv2–3 "I have loved you… Was not Esau Jacob's brother?… Yet I loved Jacob, but Esau I hated" — the book is a set of disputes: the LORD says a thing, the people answer How? or In what?, and He answers them (1:2, 6, 7; 2:14, 17). The twins were two peoples from the womb, the elder shall serve the younger (Genesis 25:23). Loved… hated is a choice made between brothers, as the law speaks of the son of the hated wife (Deuteronomy 21:17). Edom's mountains are made a desolation, as Obadiah foretold for the violence done to your brother Jacob (Obadiah 1:10). Tannot, jackals, as in a lair of jackals (Jeremiah 9:11); the Greek has dwellings. Paul quotes the verse in Romans 9:13.

  • vv4–5 "the Territory of Wickedness… The LORD is great beyond the territory of Israel" — gevul, territory, twice: Edom's land is named for its wickedness, and the LORD's greatness reaches past Israel's border. Zaam, is indignant, the verb of Zechariah 1:12, with which You have been indignant these seventy years.

  • vv6–8 "A son honors his father… the blind… the lame and the sick… Offer it, please, to your governor" — Honor your father is the commandment (Exodus 20:12), and My honor, kevodi, is from the same verb. The law forbids such animals, if it is lame or blind, any bad blemish, you shall not sacrifice it (Deuteronomy 15:21). Lechem, food, word for word bread, as the law calls the offerings the bread of your God (Leviticus 22:25). Ein ra, Nothing wrong!, is the priests' own answer, twice. Pechah, governor, the title of Zerubbabel (Haggai 1:1).

  • vv8–9 "will he be pleased with you, or show you favor?… plead with God to be gracious to us" — yissa fanekha, word for word lift up your face, and vi-chonnenu, be gracious to us, are the words of the priests' own blessing, The LORD make His face shine on you and be gracious to you. The LORD lift up His face toward you (Numbers 6:25–26), and v10 has ta'iru, light, the verb of shine. The priests who give the blessing cannot win it. Challu penei El, plead with God, as in Zechariah 7:2.

  • vv10–11 "shut the doors… from the rising of the sun to its setting My name is great among the nations" — better a temple shut than a fire lit chinnam, for nothing. The nations' praise is the psalm's, From the rising of the sun to its setting, the name of the LORD is to be praised (Psalm 113:3). Muqtar, incense is offered, and minchah tehorah, a pure offering: whether the LORD speaks of what the nations already do or of what is coming, the verse does not say.

  • vv12–14 "its fruit, its food… you sniff at it… a ruined one… I am a great King" — nivo, its fruit, is obscure. Ve-hippachtem oto, you sniff at it, word for word you blow at it, in contempt. Moshchat, ruined, the word the law gives for such animals, their ruin is in them (Leviticus 22:25). The law asks for a male without defect (Leviticus 1:3). Melekh gadol, a great King, the title the Assyrian took, the great king, the king of Assyria (2 Kings 18:19), given to the LORD.

chapters.title: The Covenant with Levi
chapters.html:
Malachi 2

A Command for the Priests

1"So now, priests, this command is for you.

2If you will not listen, and if you will not take it to heart to give glory to My name," says the LORD of hosts, "I will send the curse on you and curse your blessings. Indeed, I have already cursed them, because you do not take it to heart.

3I am about to rebuke your seed, and I will spread dung on your faces, the dung of your festivals, and you will be carried off with it.

4Then you will know that I have sent this command to you, so that My covenant with Levi may stand," says the LORD of hosts.

5"My covenant with him was life and peace, and I gave them to him; it was fear, and he feared Me and stood in awe of My name.

6True instruction was in his mouth, and no wrong was found on his lips; he walked with Me in peace and uprightness, and turned many away from iniquity.

7For the lips of a priest should guard knowledge, and people should seek instruction from his mouth, for he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts.

8But you have turned aside from the way; you have made many stumble by your instruction; you have corrupted the covenant of Levi," says the LORD of hosts.

9"So I in turn have made you despised and low before all the people, because you do not keep My ways but show partiality in the instruction."

Faithless to One Another

10Do we not all have one father? Did not one God create us? Why then do we break faith with one another, profaning the covenant of our fathers?

11Judah has broken faith; a detestable thing has been done in Israel and in Jerusalem. For Judah has profaned the holy place of the LORD, which He loves, and has married the daughter of a foreign god.

12May the LORD cut off from the tents of Jacob the man who does this, whoever he may be, even one who brings an offering to the LORD of hosts.

13This is another thing you do: you cover the altar of the LORD with tears, with weeping and groaning, because He no longer looks at the offering or accepts it with favor from your hands.

14Yet you say, "Why?" Because the LORD was witness between you and the wife of your youth, with whom you have broken faith, though she is your companion and your wife by covenant.

15Did He not make one, with a remnant of the spirit belonging to him? What was the one seeking? Offspring from God. So guard yourselves in your spirit, and let no one break faith with the wife of his youth.

16"For the man who hates and sends her away," says the LORD, the God of Israel, "covers his garment with violence," says the LORD of hosts. "So guard yourselves in your spirit, and do not break faith."

Where Is the God of Justice?

17You have wearied the LORD with your words. Yet you say, "How have we wearied Him?" By saying, "Everyone who does evil is good in the eyes of the LORD, and He delights in them," or, "Where is the God of justice?"

Notes

  • vv1–3 "curse your blessings… I am about to rebuke your seed… dung on your faces, the dung of your festivals" — the priests' blessings are the blessing they give (Numbers 6:23–26), now turned to curse. Zera, seed, the grain sown, or their offspring; the Greek reads zeroa, the shoulder, the priests' portion: I am separating the shoulder for you. Peresh, dung, the part of the sacrifice the law sends out, its dung you shall burn in fire outside the camp (Exodus 29:14): the priests will be carried out with it. Chag, festival, here the festival sacrifices.

  • vv4–7 "My covenant with Levi… life and peace… he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts" — the covenant given to Phinehas, the priest of Levi's line, I give him My covenant of peace (Numbers 25:12), and the blessing of Levi, They teach Your rules to Jacob and Your instruction to Israel (Deuteronomy 33:10). Torat emet, true instruction. Mal'akh YHWH tseva'ot, the messenger of the LORD of hosts, said of a priest, as Haggai is the LORD's messenger (Haggai 1:13), and as the book's name means My messenger (1:1).

  • vv8–9 "you have made many stumble… show partiality in the instruction" — Nos'im panim, show partiality, word for word lift faces, the words of 1:8–9: the priests want the LORD to lift His face to them while they lift faces in judgment. Nehemiah prays against those who defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites (Nehemiah 13:29).

  • vv10–12 "one father… one God… married the daughter of a foreign god… whoever he may be" — bagad, break faith, five times in vv10–16. One father is God, Is He not your Father, who acquired you, who made you (Deuteronomy 32:6). To'evah, a detestable thing. Qodesh YHWH, the holy place of the LORD, may also be the holiness of the LORD, Judah itself set apart. Bat el nekhar, the daughter of a foreign god, a woman who worships another god, as in Ezra's time, the holy seed has mixed itself with the peoples of the lands (Ezra 9:2). Er ve-oneh, word for word one who wakes and one who answers, is obscure; it seems to mean anyone at all.

  • vv13–14 "you cover the altar of the LORD with tears… the wife of your youth… your wife by covenant" — eshet ne'urekha, the wife of your youth, as in rejoice in the wife of your youth (Proverbs 5:18). Chavertekha, your companion, as in who forsakes the companion of her youth and forgets the covenant of her God (Proverbs 2:17): marriage is a covenant with God as witness.

  • vv15–16 "Did He not make one… Offspring from God… the man who hates and sends her away covers his garment with violence" — v15 is obscure. Ve-lo echad asah may be Did He not make one, the two who become one flesh (Genesis 2:24), or no one has done this who has a remnant of the spirit. Zera Elohim, offspring from God, children of a faithful marriage. Ki sane shallach: sane is he hates, shallach is send away, as the law says of divorce, he writes her a certificate of divorce… and sends her out of his house (Deuteronomy 24:1). The Greek has If, hating her, you send her away.

  • v17 "You have wearied the LORD with your words… Where is the God of justice?" — hoga'tem, wearied, as in you have wearied Me with your iniquities (Isaiah 43:24). The question is answered at once in 3:1.
